rationale:
dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=1234, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=8, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=3000, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, rationale=iter-7 CEILING-DOCUMENTATION PROBE (warm-start depth) toward iter-20 -- NOT hr-chasing. Change EXACTLY ONE knob: pretrain_epochs 3 -> 8 (deepen the amortized N2I warm-start pre-pass on the train split; everything else held at the iter-1 canonical 6-param config: warm_start=True, img_n_bf=proj_n_bf=1, all sigmas at Wagner defaults, n_iter=400, lr=5e-3, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=6). seed kept at 1234 (iter-6-confirmed stable). This is a clean single-knob A/B vs iter-1/iter-6.

STATE: CONVERGED to the 6-param structural ceiling. 6 iters all flat at SSIM ~0.9462 @1, hr 0 (PSNR ~35.6 dB, ~1 dB BELOW the LD-FBP baseline 36.56 dB): iter-1 0.946237, iter-2 (img_n_bf 1->3) 0.945237, iter-3 (img_sr 0.02->0.005) 0.946177, iter-4 (proj_sr 0.02->0.0005) 0.945745, iter-5 (warm_start OFF) 0.945955, iter-6 (seed 42->1234) 0.946157. This matches the documented dd-bf-supervised structural ceiling (capped 0.9502 with the SAME 6 BF params, every scalar flat).

FAILURE MODE (structural, not a tuning miss): the 6-param bilateral cannot beat an already-clean dense-view (2304-angle) FBP -- the half-view N2I information loss (each per-scan fit only ever sees a 1152-angle subset of the scan) exceeds what 6 trainable bilateral params can denoise, so no sigma/depth/warm_start/seed setting clears hr=0. The remaining iters to the iter-20 goal are CEILING DOCUMENTATION (probes that show WHY the ceiling holds), not optimization.

WHY THIS KNOB / NEW AXIS: all 6 prior iters probed BF sigma/depth (iter-2,3,4), warm_start presence on/off (iter-5), and RNG/val-draw (iter-6). pretrain_epochs has stayed at 3 every iter -- it is the ONE remaining untried structural axis: warm-start QUALITY/DEPTH, distinct from warm-start PRESENCE. iter-5 already proved warm_start ON vs OFF is inert (0.9462 vs 0.9460), but that tested only whether the warm-start exists, not whether a *better-conditioned, more-trained* amortized init shifts the per-scan fit. Note the campaign-state insight that raising per-scan n_iter HURTS the U-Net N2I via per-scan overfit (no early-stop in _fit_one_scene); the 6-param bilateral physically CANNOT overfit one scan, so the analogous probe here is to improve the INIT, not the per-scan step count. pretrain_epochs 3->8 gives the per-scan Adam fit a deeper amortized N2I starting point.

EXPECTATION (this is the success condition for a ceiling-documentation probe): a deeper warm-start (8 ep) is expected to land at essentially the SAME ~0.9462 @1, hr 0. A flat result CONFIRMS the ceiling is invariant to warm-start depth -- the 6-param BF converges to the same below-FBP per-scan optimum regardless of how well the amortized init is trained, because the limit is the BF's 6-param capacity vs the 2304-view FBP and the half-view N2I info loss, NOT init conditioning. By construction this adds NO trainable capacity and does NOT change the per-scan optimization regime, so it cannot escape the ceiling -- it can only bound it along the warm-start-depth axis. This is ceiling-documentation toward the iter-20 hard stop, not hr-chasing.

Per-image N2I (commit 1f4c3394): short amortized warm-start pre-pass (now 8 ep x 200 train) then per-scan Adam fit (400 steps) on each val scan's OWN half-angle measurements (GT-free), scored by evaluate_calibrated on the SAME L277 val scenes as every other Mayo method. NOT amortized train-then-forward. Wall <=15 min target: iter-1 ran 469s at pretrain_epochs=3/val_n=6; +5 warm-start epochs x 200 train x ~0.5 s ~ +50-80s, well within the 1h sbatch wall and the <=15 min soft target.
